en: Regarding the discussion on the revival of the Tiantai teachings:
the doctrinal systems of the Mountain School have been transmitted for a long time, and the standard texts of both the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna collections remain extant.
Why, then, is it specifically said that Dharma Master Zhili of Siming "revived" them? It is said: although the standard texts remain, those who were deluded held divergent views.

Outside the mountain [tradition], another school arose that produced groundless and forced interpretations; since its transmission was erroneous and its insights were further deviant, the teachings and contemplations of this one house gradually sank into oblivion.
Is this not what the ancients meant when they said, "The Way is like a suspended thread pulling a stone"?
It was thanks to Master Siming that it was revived, so that the general outline of the teachings and contemplations of this one house...
From that time until the present day, all people have received his bounty. I have long harbored a private doubt regarding this:

the entire world claims that Siming (Zhiyuan) "revived" the Tiantai teachings and contemplations (*jiaoguan*), yet they do not know what this so-called "revival" actually means. I wonder how this doctrine of "revival" is explained;

please attempt to set it forth for me. Some might say that it refers to the totality and differentiation of the three thousand phenomena in both principle and phenomena (*shili sanqian zongbie sheng*).
Is it not the case that the teachings of Zhongxing (the "Restoration") are precisely those found here in the personage of Shenzun? Now, I say this is not so.
One should know that as for the Way of Zhongxing in Siming, who else but Master Ciyun of India could have known it? His *Zhiyao xu* states:

"Regarding the provisional and the real within the gates of the Teaching, it is here that they are now distinguished; the principle of the distinct [truth] following conditions is of the same category."

By observing that which the Way relies upon, we see here how successive generations have collectively been deluded. Thus, the reason for establishing the *Zhijiao* (Pointing to the Essentials) is clear.

How magnificent are the words of India—these can certainly be trusted! We know, therefore, that within the *Zhijiao chao*, the principle of "the distinct truth following conditions" (*bierli suiyuan*) establishes the revival of our school’s teaching of the Perfect and Sudden;
and the "contemplation of the provisional within the five aggregates" (*liyin guanwang*) reveals our school’s method of contemplation regarding the objective realm.
The Way consists of these two teachings alone; this is the core intent behind the revival of the doctrinal and contemplative systems (*jiaoguan*).
Later generations, failing to grasp this essential point, have pointed to others, claiming that those who could transmit the Way of Zhongxing from Siming were far removed from it. A doubt is raised:
By what principle is the teaching of "the distinct principle following conditions" (*bierli suiyuan*) identified as the doctrine of Zhongxing? This is because the Shanwai faction adheres to it.

Those of the Tiantai school all claim that the doctrine of "evolving according to conditions" (*suiyuan*) as taught in the Final Teaching (*zhongjiao*) of the Mahāyāna by the Xianshou school is identical to the meaning of "evolving according to conditions" in our own school’s Perfect Teaching (*yuanjiao*).
They thereby seek to undermine the discourse on the Perfect and Sudden (*yuantun*) of our own tradition by equating it with that Final Teaching.

How much more so when that [Xianshou] school possesses both Sudden and Perfect teachings; this renders the claim that our own school can withstand and surpass the doctrines of a hundred schools and transcend all other explanations utterly untenable.

"Abiding in that lower [stage]"—the Four Ming masters followed this principle and opened it up, asserting that the Perfect Teaching (Zhengjiao) of the Mahāyāna, which accords with conditions, is identical to the specific doctrine of our own school.

Furthermore, when compared to the Sudden Teaching (Dunjiao) and the Perfect Teaching (Yuanjiao), since those do not discuss the principle of "identity-inclusion" (*ji*), their meaning cannot be fully established;
thus, it is only through the specific doctrine of our own school that the meaning of what we proclaim—the Perfect-Sudden teaching—is revealed as transcending both identity and inclusion.

The Master of Four Clarifications (Siming) surpassed all other expositions; indeed, the fact that he alone fully elucidated this very point makes it evident that the revival of our school’s teachings lies precisely here.

Thus, the reason the practice of *vipaśyanā* (contemplation) was revived is also because the "School Outside the Mountains" failed to understand the principle of the object of contemplation (*vipaśyanā-viṣaya*) within *śamatha-vipaśyanā*.

Instead, they took the single thought-moment (*ekacitta-kṣaṇa*) to be the true mind and did not establish the realms of the five aggregates (*pañca-skandha*) as the object of contemplation. Siming rebuked them, saying: "Great... [The text here implies a severe condemnation].
Because the fundamental principle had been lost, he established "insubstantial delusion" (*yinwang*) as the object of contemplation to manifest the wondrous principle;

thus it is said that pointing to the "momentary mind" (*ji'er xin*) constitutes the essential point for understanding the phenomena, penetrating the principle, and practicing the contemplations. Is this not a revival of the discourse on "objects and contemplations" (*jingguan*)?

Only after grasping this meaning can one discuss the teachings on the Middle Way and the relationship between doctrine and contemplation in the tradition of Zhili of Siming, such as [the application of] the Three Truths.

The three thousand phenomena of principle and fact, the general and the specific, the realms with and without form, the three contemplations, the three bodies, and the lifespan—these are all recorded in the *Chapters and Records* (*Shanji*), from which they may be understood.
I address scholars: you who study the teachings and contemplations of Emperor Xuanzong must recognize their source and transmission;
you must not merely follow them blindly.
Discourse on the Revival of Teaching and Contemplation (Concluded)
